acceptance_criteria: iverilog compiles submission/recovered_rtl.v plus an evaluator-authored testbench without errors.
For the shipped stimulus.txt sequence, recovered_fsm's out sequence matches the reference netlist's out sequence on every cycle.
For >=5 hidden pseudo-random sequences (length >=64) and >=2 adversarial sequences designed around the '1011' boundary cases, recovered_fsm's out matches the reference netlist's out on every cycle.
Static banned-construct scan finds no direct instantiation of primitives.v gate modules and no textual copy of flattened_netlist.v content inside recovered_rtl.v.
recovered_fsm module has exactly ports clk, rst, in, out with correct 1-bit directions.
ground_truth: The flattened netlist implements a 4-state Moore FSM that detects the non-overlapping serial pattern '1011' on input 'in', asserting 'out'=1 for exactly one clock cycle when the pattern completes, then returning to the initial state to search again. Internally the netlist uses two flip-flops (state encoded as S0=00, S1=01, S2=10, S3=11 in the gate netlist, but the encoding is obscured by XOR-mixed gate logic and non-mnemonic net names) plus combinational next-state and output logic built from NAND/NOR/XOR primitives instantiated from primitives.v. A correct recovery need not use the same encoding, only equivalent behavior.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Static banned-construct scan (fail-on-presence only) of submission/recovered_rtl.v for instantiations of primitive module names defined in inputs/primitives.v (e.g. NAND2, NOR2, XOR2, DFF) or direct textual inclusion of inputs/flattened_netlist.v; presence causes FAIL regardless of simulated correctness.
security_requirements.requirement: The recovered RTL must not merely re-embed the original gate-level netlist verbatim (e.g. by wrapping primitives.v gates inside recovered_fsm); it must be expressed at the word/register level using synthesizable behavioral constructs, so that the recovery step reflects genuine structural understanding rather than pass-through obfuscation.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Interface conformance check: recovered_fsm must have exactly the four ports clk, rst, in, out with correct directions and 1-bit widths; extra ports cause FAIL.
security_requirements.requirement: The recovered module must not leak or depend on any internal debug/backdoor signal that might exist in the flattened netlist beyond the public clk/rst/in/out interface.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Evaluator generates hidden randomized and adversarial stimulus sequences at grading time (not shipped in inputs/) and compares cycle-by-cycle output against the reference netlist simulation.
security_requirements.requirement: Behavioral equivalence must hold under adversarial/edge-case input sequences (e.g. repeated resets mid-pattern, back-to-back overlapping near-matches like '10110111011'), not just the sample stimulus, to rule out a submission that overfits to the shipped stimulus file.

threat_model: A flattened, gate-level netlist with meaningless net names (e.g. n12, n47) and gate-mixed state encoding obscures the control intent of the design, preventing engineers from auditing, verifying, or safely modifying the controller logic. This mirrors reverse-engineering-resistant obfuscation used to hide IP or malicious backdoors in third-party sequential IP cores.
